messages.author: cc3e8d7d11a99465
messages.subject: interpretation of partial measurement invariance
parts:
Dear all,

Is it okay to work with the raw data when reaching partial measurement invariance?
When following the article of Steenkamp et. al (1998), partial measurement invariance is sufficient to compare latent means across the group. But when following Scholderer et. al (2005), you first have to correct for the bias.
So my question; is it okay to assume that I can pool the data of the groups and that I can compare the latent means when I reach partial metric and scalar invariance?
If not, what is the best way to handle this in lavaan?

Thank you for your help.
Kind regards,
Silke

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: interpretation of partial measurement invariance
parts: So my question; is it okay to assume that I can pool the data of the groups and that I can compare the latent means when I reach partial metric and scalar invariance?

These are 2 questions.  As Steenkamp et al. (1998) discuss, the answer to your second question is "yes."  But your first questions confuses me.  By "pool the data of the groups" do you mean that you fit a single-group model to all data (i.e., from both groups, but ignoring the grouping variable)?  I believe the only time that is justified is when all parameters (factor loadings, intercepts, residual variances, latent variances/covariances/means) can be constrained to equality across groups.  Also, if you ignore grouping, then you can't compare group latent-means.  If you mean to fit a single-group model to all data and include a group-indicator variable (e.g., dummy code) to predict the latent mean, that model assumes that residual variances are equal across groups.

Terry

parts:
Dear Terry,

Thank you for your respons.
Actually, I just want to be sure that I can pool my data from the different countries so that I can do a cluster analysis on this pooled data and subsequently describe the clusters without taking into account the variable "country".

Kind regards,
Silke
